correctness.rationale: Homogeneity identifies one-types with triangle-free vertex subsets. A complete loop over all simple graph edge masks on each labelled set of order zero through six, with explicit K4 exclusion and every vertex subset, checks integer cross-multiplied normalized inequalities. Only 72 six-vertex labelled exceptions arise, each with sorted degrees (3,3,3,3,3,5), forcing the five-rim wheel. The independent wheel calculation gives exact coefficients and a normalized gap of 1/72. The proof is finite and does not extrapolate beyond order six.

value.rationale: The coefficients are a canonical stratification of complete one-types by the number of positive relations to named parameters. Binomial normalization measures the proportion of allowed k-neighborhoods and tests whether these proportions obey the log-concavity/negative-dependence paradigm. A sharp first obstruction with complete uniqueness and a minimal structural witness is a natural boundary, not an arbitrary numerical slice; it separates edge-forbidden dependence behavior from triangular-clique constraints in a classical homogeneous graph. The result has a reproducible exhaustive certificate and exact rational witness.
